title: The Long Way Home: September 1951
logline: A twenty-one-year-old naval aviator launches from USS Essex, strikes a cable during a low-level armed-reconnaissance run, and must hold a crippled Panther together long enough to reach friendly territory and eject.
authoredInvariants: Armstrong launches from USS Essex as a VF-51 Panther pilot on an armed-reconnaissance sortie.
Major John Carpenter leads the flight.
The required low-level attack route intersects physical cable geometry.
Cable contact removes a substantial portion of the right wing and creates persistent asymmetric flight.
Armstrong and Carpenter determine that slowing for a landing is unsafe.
Armstrong carries the aircraft south into friendly territory before ejecting.
The ejection, parachute descent and ground recovery complete the playable sequence.
No mission dialogue foreshadows Apollo, the Moon or Armstrong's later fame.

owns: Deck and launch checks that are exposed as controls.
Formation position, route discipline, attack-run control and terrain clearance.
Immediate control response after the cable strike.
Airspeed, roll, yaw, altitude and engine management in the damaged aircraft.
Execution of the ejection preparation and ejection action.
The quality of the flight as recorded for replay and debrief.
doesNotOwn: Whether the historical cable strike occurs.
Whether the damaged Panther is judged unsafe to land.
Whether the story becomes a counterfactual biography.
The documented identities of Armstrong, Carpenter, VF-51 or USS Essex.
Dialogue, camera, damage or recovery facts not supported by simulation events.
plotBreakingDivergence: Abandoning or bypassing the required attack corridor.
Missing the authored cable contact after entering its terminal approach gate.
Crashing before the damaged-flight beat can advance.
Leaving the damaged-flight route or ejecting before the friendly-territory gate.
Failing an ejection action in a way that would replace the documented recovery with an alternate death.
playerAgency.retryPolicy: Restore the nearest completed narrative checkpoint with identical mission seed, authored conditions and disclosed reconstruction status; do not canonize the failed attempt as an alternate historical outcome.

cast.operationalRole: VF-51 F9F Panther pilot and player character
cast.dramaticFunction: Make the story emerge from a young pilot's technical attention, aircraft handling and procedural composure rather than retrospective hero narration.
cast.knowledgeBoundary: He knows only what he can see, feel in the controls, hear over the radio or infer from the Panther's instruments and Carpenter's inspection.
cast.dialoguePolicy: Use sourced words when available and otherwise only restrained procedural reconstruction; never invent private thought, political exposition, moral instruction or Moon foreshadowing.
cast.voicePolicy: Use an original disclosed synthetic performance appropriate to a young Midwestern U.S. naval aviator; never clone, match or instruct the model to imitate Neil Armstrong's recorded voice.

cast.operationalRole: USAF exchange officer and flight lead
cast.dramaticFunction: Provide the external damage inspection and professional second judgment that turns a damaged-flight problem into the decision to eject.
cast.knowledgeBoundary: He can report what is visible from formation and what the flight's radio exchange establishes; he does not know hidden airframe state.
cast.dialoguePolicy: No quotation is locked until supported by a transcript, oral history or clearly declared procedural reconstruction.
cast.voicePolicy: Use an original disclosed synthetic performance for a mature U.S. military pilot; do not imitate a real recording or use celebrity resemblance as direction.

cast.operationalRole: Plane handlers, launch crew and flight-deck control
cast.dramaticFunction: Establish that the sortie begins inside a practiced human machine before narrowing to two aircraft over the target.
cast.knowledgeBoundary: The role knows deck state, launch state and visible aircraft condition only.
cast.dialoguePolicy: Prefer hand signals, machinery and period procedure; add named or spoken lines only after cruise records or procedure sources support them.
cast.voicePolicy: Operational voices are original performances and remain unnamed until the historical record identifies a speaker.

cast.operationalRole: Personnel who recover Armstrong after descent
cast.dramaticFunction: Return the story from machinery and sky to an ordinary human-scale ending.
cast.knowledgeBoundary: The role knows only the visible descent, landing and local recovery conditions.
cast.dialoguePolicy: Armstrong's retrospective account identifies Goodell Warren and a jeep near Pohang/K-3; do not invent words, exact location, vehicle appearance or interaction while independent corroboration remains open.
cast.voicePolicy: No voice is cast until the ground-recovery source gap is resolved.

beats.title: Essex
beats.dramaticPurpose: Introduce Armstrong as one young pilot inside VF-51's practiced carrier operation and establish the Panther as a handled machine.
beats.playerTask: Complete the exposed launch checks, hold the aircraft correctly and accept the straight-deck catapult shot.

enterWhen: The mission lifecycle is active and the Panther is secured on the Essex launch station.
completeWhen: The carrier catapult reports launch complete and the player aircraft is airborne.
failWhen: The aircraft is lost or leaves the authored launch envelope before the catapult event completes.

evidenceCapture: Checklist actions and omissions.
Launch control state and catapult event.
Aircraft attitude, speed and clearance through the first ten airborne seconds.

beats.title: Join
beats.dramaticPurpose: Move from the carrier's collective routine to Armstrong's position on Carpenter's wing and reveal the Korean coast without exposition.
beats.playerTask: Join Carpenter, preserve formation spacing and cross the coast on the assigned route.

completeWhen: The player crosses the authored coast gate inside the bounded formation envelope.
failWhen: The player loses the lead, leaves the route volume or loses the aircraft.

evidenceCapture: Formation range and bearing history.
Route-gate entry and exit times.
Player-visible weather and coast landmarks.

beats.title: Into the valley
beats.dramaticPurpose: Turn Korea's mountain geometry into workload and narrow the player's attention before the attack.
beats.playerTask: Descend with the flight, maintain terrain clearance and follow the valley toward the target area.

enterWhen: The coast gate is complete and Carpenter enters the inland route.
completeWhen: The player enters the armed-reconnaissance target area within the authored altitude and route envelope.
failWhen: Terrain contact, route abandonment or sustained separation from the flight prevents target-area entry.

evidenceCapture: Radar altitude, vertical speed and terrain-clearance history.
Route conformity and formation position.
Rendered terrain and cable visibility evidence available to the player.

beats.title: Armed reconnaissance
beats.dramaticPurpose: Give the sortie a concrete operational task and create the ordinary control workload that carries the Panther onto the cable line.
beats.playerTask: Follow Carpenter through the required target run, employ only against the validated military objective and recover into the exit valley.

enterWhen: The target-area gate is complete and the lead begins the authored run.
completeWhen: The player completes the required employment gate and enters the cable corridor on the canonical egress line.
failWhen: The player abandons the run, attacks a prohibited object, loses the aircraft or fails to enter the canonical egress line.

evidenceCapture: Target identity and authorization evidence visible at employment.
Weapon release, gun events and aim geometry.
Exit-route pose, speed and control state.

beats.title: The cable
beats.dramaticPurpose: Transform an almost invisible terrain obstacle into the incident that changes the sortie from attack to survival.
beats.playerTask: Fly the required egress corridor and respond immediately when physical cable contact tears the right wing.

enterWhen: The attack-run completion event places the aircraft inside the terminal cable corridor.
completeWhen: Authoritative swept collision reports player contact with a cable and the right-wing damage state is committed.
failWhen: The player leaves the terminal corridor, misses the required cable contact or loses the aircraft before damage authority commits.

evidenceCapture: Cable identity, contact point, relative velocity and collision impulse.
Detached geometry and committed aerodynamic damage parameters.
Player control state immediately before and after contact.

beats.title: Hold it
beats.dramaticPurpose: Make the missing wing a sustained aerodynamic problem rather than a cosmetic story flag.
beats.playerTask: Arrest the roll, avoid terrain and establish a controllable speed and attitude with the damaged Panther.

enterWhen: The right-wing damage state is committed.
completeWhen: The aircraft remains airborne and inside bounded roll, terrain-clearance and controllability limits for the authored stabilization interval.
failWhen: Terrain contact, unrecoverable departure or numerical terminal state occurs before stabilization completes.

evidenceCapture: Roll rate, sideslip, control input and remaining authority.
Airspeed, altitude, clearance and load factor.
Time to establish the bounded controllable state.

beats.title: No landing
beats.dramaticPurpose: Let two pilots reason from visible damage and handling evidence rather than having narration announce the answer.
beats.playerTask: Hold a steady inspection formation while Carpenter assesses the wing, then acknowledge the decision to avoid a landing attempt.

enterWhen: Damaged-flight stabilization is complete and Carpenter reaches the inspection station.
completeWhen: Carpenter's observer-safe inspection state and the player's demonstrated low-speed handling evidence support the no-landing decision.
failWhen: The player cannot hold the inspection envelope, loses the aircraft or attempts an unauthorized landing route.

evidenceCapture: Inspection formation geometry and duration.
Damage facts visible to Carpenter.
Airspeed, roll authority and stability evidence used for the decision.

beats.title: South
beats.dramaticPurpose: Turn the long return over hostile terrain into sustained concentration and make friendly territory an earned physical boundary.
beats.playerTask: Follow Carpenter south while preserving control, altitude and enough margin to reach the friendly-territory ejection area.

enterWhen: The ejection decision event is committed.
completeWhen: The player crosses the friendly-territory gate inside the damaged-flight safety envelope.
failWhen: The aircraft is lost, the player leaves the southbound route or ejects before the friendly-territory gate.

evidenceCapture: Route, altitude, airspeed, roll and control-margin history.
Friendly-territory boundary crossing.
Any loss-of-control episodes and recoveries.

beats.title: Prepare
beats.dramaticPurpose: Convert ejection from a button press into a short, dangerous procedure performed while still flying the aircraft.
beats.playerTask: Point the Panther into the authored safe disposal corridor, establish the required ejection envelope and complete the exposed preparation actions.

completeWhen: Aircraft pose and speed are inside the authored ejection envelope and every exposed preparation action is committed.
failWhen: The player leaves the disposal corridor, loses the aircraft or exhausts the recoverable ejection envelope.

evidenceCapture: Checklist action order and omissions.
Aircraft pose, speed, vertical rate and terrain clearance.
Disposal-corridor alignment and elapsed margin.

beats.title: Punch out
beats.dramaticPurpose: Make separation from the aircraft abrupt, mechanical and physically consequential without spectacle.
beats.playerTask: Initiate ejection only after the ready state and survive seat separation and parachute deployment.

completeWhen: Authoritative ejection, aircraft separation, seat separation and parachute deployment events complete in order.
failWhen: The ejection action is attempted outside the ready state or physical separation cannot complete inside the validated safety model.

evidenceCapture: Ejection action tick and readiness state.
Seat acceleration, clearance and separation sequence.
Aircraft and pilot trajectories through parachute deployment.

beats.title: Back over land
beats.dramaticPurpose: Replace engine noise and cockpit workload with wind, height and the exposed human body as the damaged Panther departs.
beats.playerTask: Manage the limited parachute actions exposed by the sourced equipment model and prepare for ground contact.

completeWhen: The pilot reaches the authoritative ground-contact state inside the friendly recovery area.
failWhen: The parachute or pilot reaches an unrecoverable state before the friendly ground-contact event.

evidenceCapture: Wind, canopy state and pilot trajectory.
Landing-area surface and contact state.
The damaged aircraft's separately integrated terminal trajectory.

beats.title: Recovery
beats.dramaticPurpose: End at human scale with survival and ordinary recovery rather than triumph, score or retrospective destiny.
beats.playerTask: Remain present through the short recovery beat and then enter the evidence-backed debrief.

enterWhen: The friendly pilot ground-contact event is committed.
completeWhen: The bounded quiet interval and sourced recovery action complete.
failWhen: Source review blocks the authored recovery action or the authoritative pilot state is not recoverable.

evidenceCapture: Pilot recovery state and recovery-area identity.
Quiet-interval timing and skip request, if any.
Complete ordered narrative-event and flight-recorder streams.

cameraRules: Player-controlled flight remains in the normal flight camera; directed exterior cameras may appear only during non-control-critical setup, ejection transition or aftermath.
The cable is never hidden by a cinematic camera cut at the moment collision authority evaluates it.
Camera shake conveys impulse but cannot obscure the first recoverable control cue.
Parachute transition preserves spatial continuity between aircraft, seat and pilot.
audioRules: Cockpit, engine, airflow, cable impact, structure and ejection mechanics carry the drama before music.
Radio remains sparse, operational and subordinate to aircraft control.
No generated voice imitates a historical person's recording.
A quiet interval follows parachute opening and returns again at ground recovery.
Production acceptance uses silent audio QA unless the user explicitly requests audible review.
interfaceRules: The briefing labels the sequence a historical reconstruction and exposes material disputes without front-loading an essay.
Fixed-history restart copy says that the reconstruction cannot continue from the divergent state.
Objectives describe operational actions, not narrative spoilers.
The debrief separates documented event, modeled reconstruction and player performance.
accessibilityRules: All radio and spoken procedure has synchronized captions with stable speaker labels.
Cable visibility has a high-contrast accessibility treatment that preserves its physical location and does not move collision truth.
Ejection preparation supports remappable actions, hold/toggle choice and extended timing without changing story order.
Reduced-motion mode limits camera impulse and transition motion while preserving collision and control information.
Difficulty assistance changes control support and timing margins, never historical claims or hidden obstacle geometry.
localizationRules: Store line identity, source text, performance text and localized caption separately.
Do not fake Korean or American accents as localization shorthand.
Period aviation terms retain a reviewed glossary and are not machine-expanded into modern phraseology.
On-screen dates remain September 1951 until the dossier resolves or preserves the source conflict.

tests.proves: The sequence document is structurally complete and rejects undeclared fields.
Every non-fiction beat and cast assertion closes through the approved mission dossier.

Restoring any narrative checkpoint reproduces the same seed, authored conditions and initial state hash.
Only authoritative swept cable contact commits wing damage and presentation cannot create the incident.

Carpenter's inspection and radio use only geometry and observer-visible damage evidence.
Aircraft, seat, pilot, parachute and ground recovery transition through authoritative states without duplicate or missing events.
Replay preserves the pre-strike approach, collision, damage, control response, decision and ejection without rerunning physics.
Every critical spoken fact is available through synchronized captions and a non-audio mission cue.
Generated voices are disclosed original performances and no prompt, voice or asset imitates a historical person.
The real audio graph, event scheduling, clip hashes and cleanup pass with destination gain clamped.
Cable, wing damage, lead position, ejection envelope and terrain remain legible in every approved weather and quality tier.
Narrative scenery, damage, ejection and presentation remain inside the existing frame-time and asset budgets.
A clean production build can complete the full fixed-history sequence, debrief it and restart without fatal render, input or audio waits.
